stories.body: Congress removed Santiago Peña from office after the collapse of Ueno Bank left roughly 2.9 million customers unable to access their accounts. Prosecutors placed Peña under house arrest amid an investigation into alleged financial crimes and influence peddling; he has said his former investment in Ueno’s parent company was purely financial. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as president.
stories.headline: Paraguay’s president impeached and placed under house arrest after bank collapse

stories.body: Donald Trump said US forces struck an Iranian air defence system on Friday, describing the attack as minor. Iranian state media reported two missile strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz and said Iran had shot down a US drone. Trump also claimed progress in talks with Tehran, while Qatar, which is mediating, disputed reports that negotiations had failed.
stories.headline: Trump confirms new US strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island

stories.body: The African National Congress had 31.8% of the national vote with more than 80% of ballots counted, nearly 14 percentage points below its 2021 local election result. The Democratic Alliance had 24.1%, while former president Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto weSizwe party had 9.3%. Coalition talks are expected to determine control of major cities, and final results are due Sunday.
stories.headline: South Africa’s ANC faces defeat in local elections

stories.body: A court in Mombasa sentenced Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison after convicting him of murdering 190 children and one adult. Prosecutors said his followers were ordered to starve themselves and their children; Mackenzie denied forcing the victims to starve. More than 400 bodies have been recovered from the Shakahola forest, and investigations into other deaths continue.
stories.headline: Kenyan sect leader sentenced to 200 years for murder of 190 children and one adult

stories.body: In preliminary findings, the European Commission said TikTok’s recommendation system can repeatedly expose young and vulnerable users to content about subjects such as body image and isolation, potentially worsening mental health problems. Officials said tools such as the “not interested” button did not adequately prevent similar content from returning. TikTok disputed the findings and said it gives users control over their feeds.
stories.headline: EU says TikTok failed to protect users from harmful content loops

stories.body: Donald Trump named Stephen Miller, a central architect of his administration’s mass deportation programme, as his new chief of staff. Miller has faced criticism over immigration enforcement, including after ICE agents fatally shot two protesters in Minneapolis in January. His promotion drew alarm from leaders of industries that rely on immigrant workers.
stories.headline: Trump names Stephen Miller White House chief of staff

stories.body: The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, with hiring across several industries showing unexpected strength in the labour market.
stories.headline: US economy added 165,000 jobs in October

stories.body: The CDC reported 5,182 confirmed measles cases so far in 2026, more than double the 2025 total, with children and teenagers accounting for about 59% of cases. The agency counted four deaths, fewer than state officials have reported; Pennsylvania alone has reported six measles-associated deaths. US kindergarten vaccination coverage has fallen from 95.2% in 2019–20 to 92.4% in 2025–26.
stories.headline: US measles cases exceed 5,000, the highest number since 1991

stories.body: Voters approved measures restricting transgender youth sports and treatment despite Democratic gains in the midterm elections. Colorado and Washington joined states banning transgender girls from girls’ sports teams, while Arizona and Nebraska strengthened existing bans.
stories.headline: Voters approve restrictions on transgender youth despite Democratic midterm gains

stories.body: The European Public Prosecutor’s Office is investigating possible fraud involving EU funds for safety, signalling and communications upgrades on the Madrid–Seville high-speed line. Investigators sought documents from rail infrastructure manager Adif, the railway safety agency and the Court of Auditors after the October 28 crash in Urda killed 69 people. The financial investigation is separate from the inquiry into the cause of the collision; prosecutors are also investigating contracts after January’s fatal Adamuz crash.
stories.headline: European prosecutors investigate possible rail contract fraud after Urda crash

stories.body: Anti-corruption prosecutors have asked a judge to proceed against former transport ministry adviser Koldo García, businessman Víctor de Aldama and former Adif president Isabel Pardo de Vera, among others, in a branch of the Koldo case. The allegations include influence peddling, money laundering and bribery, depending on the defendant. The judge must decide whether the case proceeds to trial.
stories.headline: Prosecutors seek trial for Koldo García and others in separate corruption case

stories.body: Pedro Sánchez returned to the campaign trail in Valencia ahead of Spain’s November 29 election, opening the event with a minute of silence for the 69 people killed in the Urda crash. He defended the government’s response, including the resignation of transport minister Óscar Puente, and called for investment in public services. Sánchez also urged voters to mobilise behind the PSOE against the right and far right.
stories.headline: Sánchez resumes election campaign after Urda rail disaster

stories.body: Spain has ordered mills to store 12% of their olive oil production, temporarily withholding an estimated 188,000 tonnes until September 30, 2027. The government says a large harvest and existing stocks threaten farmers’ returns, but the competition regulator warns the measure could raise consumer prices and reduce choice. Some Catalan producers also oppose it, saying it does not reflect conditions in areas without surpluses.
stories.headline: Spain orders 12% of olive oil production withheld to support prices

stories.body: During the November 10 and 12 drivers’ strikes, Catalunya will guarantee 33% of normal Rodalies and regional train service, rising to 66% during peak hours of 6–9:30 a.m. and 5–8:30 p.m. The November 10 strike is planned for the full day; November 12 stoppages are partial. A separate general strike on November 11 will affect public transport, with minimum service of 25% during peak hours.
stories.headline: Catalunya sets minimum Rodalies service for train drivers’ strikes

stories.body: The Cursa de Bombers 10-kilometre race on November 8 will bring traffic restrictions and changes to 31 bus routes, mainly in Ciutat Vella, Eixample and Sants-Montjuïc. The main disruptions are expected from roughly 6 a.m. to 3 p.m., with the race starting at 8:50 a.m. for uniformed firefighters and 9 a.m. for other runners. TMB recommends using the metro.
stories.headline: Cursa de Bombers will close Barcelona streets and divert buses on Sunday

stories.body: A study commissioned by SOS Costa Brava calls for better protection and management of Albera Marítima, the bays of Roses and Pals, and the Empordà 2 marine area. It identifies gaps in surveillance, regulation and coordination, and argues that the areas could connect existing protected habitats. The group plans to submit the study to the Catalan and Spanish governments.
stories.headline: SOS Costa Brava calls for stronger protection of four marine areas

stories.body: Barcelona has fined Bicing operator UTE Pedalem €150,000 over bicycle availability and maintenance failures, amid complaints involving batteries, brakes and the app. The city also announced a €5.8 million improvement plan, including more maintenance staff, replacement batteries and 400 reserve bikes. It plans to convert the remaining 3,000 mechanical bikes to electric during the first half of 2027.
stories.headline: Barcelona fines Bicing operator €150,000 over service failures
